extracted.intended_audience: research scientists and practitioners (botany, marine biology, and early telecommunications); readers of Nature
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and normative standards for conducting, reporting, and interpreting scientific research (illustrated here with examples from marine investigations, wireless telegraphy, and botany). Emphasises physiological/physico-chemical approaches, careful inference from evidence, standardisation, and appropriate technical choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and accessibility of scientific summaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Being well written, illustrated by good charts and plates, and demanding no great previous knowledge from the reader, it is one of those accurate yet popular accounts which, by educating public opinion in the utility of research, possess a real public value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports should aim to be accurate yet accessible: good prose, clear illustrations and charts, and avoidance of unnecessary technical obscurity increase public value and understanding; note that language choice can restrict readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical scientific aim (rational exploitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The aim of the work to be, in the terms of a resolution ... 'to prepare for the rational exploitation of the sea on a scientific basis.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific programmes addressing natural resources should state practical aims tied to rational, evidence-based exploitation; practical questions (e.g., over-fishing) should guide parts of the research agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use and improvement of market statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Speak hopefully of the value of market statistics, recognise the recent improvements in English methods of collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistical (market) data are valuable for problems like over-fishing; improving methods of collection strengthens the basis for scientific and policy conclusions, but must be complemented by biological investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid premature policy proposals; base policy on fully sifted evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: To make any proposal for restrictive legislation before the International Council has fully sifted the evidence ... seems premature, and, from the representatives of a country not greatly interested in trawling, even a little out of place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legislative or regulatory recommendations should follow thorough, preferably international, evaluation of the evidence; policymakers and scientists should avoid proposing restrictions until evidence has been fully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: National inshore size limits and landing restrictions (recommended)
rubrics_metrics.description: Advise that each country fix an inshore size limit independently, while no plaice should be landed from off-shore grounds of less length than 38 cm., that limit to be gradually increased . to 33 cm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific fisheries-management recommendations are proposed, but their practicability and enforceability need explicit consideration (the authors are silent on enforcement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardisation and international cooperation in hydrography
rubrics_metrics.description: Hydrography gained much from cooperation; the standardising of instruments ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperative international work and standardisation of instruments and methods improve the comparability, quality, and utility of hydrographic and related data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages of tuning in wireless telegraphy (distance and syntony)
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the two distinct advantages of tuning, namely, greater distance and syntony, or responding to only one definite note.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tuning receiving circuits (e.g., adding a condenser) increases reception distance and selectivity (syntony); technical design should exploit tuning where range and selectivity matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose transmission method to match speed and syntony requirements (arc vs spark)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the arc method the oscillations are maintained continuously of unvarying amplitude ... in the spark method ... the oscillations ... die away rapidly, making only a limited number of oscillations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Arc-method transmitters (continuous oscillations) allow precise syntony and are well suited to very high signalling speeds; spark-method transmitters produce damping trains and may require high sparking rates for comparable speeds—method choice should depend on required speed and operational constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical limitations of the spark method for high-speed, long-distance signalling
rubrics_metrics.description: The dot of the Morse alphabet must at least occupy the average time required to charge the condenser or aerial and produce one spark ... obliged in the spark method to use a high rate of sparking for high-speed signalling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise that spark systems face engineering difficulties when high-speed signalling and high power for long distances are both required; design trade-offs and apparatus improvements are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receiver interoperability and compliance with international conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Berlin Convention ... imposes an obligation on all commercial stations to inter-communicate without regard to the make or system of transmitting apparatus employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To achieve interoperability, transmitters (e.g., spark stations) should send long trains of waves and systems should be designed to permit cross-system reception; technical standards should support legal/international obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approaches to wireless telephony (amplitude and frequency modulation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose that we can vary the intensity of the oscillations ... by employing an ordinary microphone to modify the current through the transmitting arc ... Another method ... consists in causing the microphone to vary the frequency of the oscillations ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wireless telephony can be pursued by varying amplitude (intensity) or frequency of carrier oscillations; receivers must be sensitive to the chosen modulation (e.g., point-detectors and telephones) and experiments suggest promising early results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain a physiological conception of morphology
rubrics_metrics.description: A physiological conception of morphological phenomena is the one that to me seems to afford the broadest outlook ... It serves to check a tendency towards mere formalism ... and to correct ... superficial teleology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret morphological features via physiological (chemical/physical) mechanisms rather than purely descriptive/formal or teleological accounts; this approach fosters deeper explanatory power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analyse biological problems into chemical and physical components
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly attempting to analyse our problems, as far as may be possible, into their chemical and physical components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking problems into underlying physico-chemical factors enables controlled manipulation and better causal understanding; this is the recommended methodological stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goal of scientific inquiry: ascertain cause and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: The goal of all scientific inquiry lies in the ultimate ascertaining of cause and effect, and only with this knowledge can we hope to get control over the results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasise causal explanation rather than descriptive correlation; experimental design and interpretation should aim at causal inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject uncritical teleological/anthropomorphic explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not enough to explain the appearance of a structure on the ground of its utility; properly speaking, such attempts ... actually tend to bar the way of inquiry just where scientific investigation ought to commence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept 'adaptedness' as an explanation: instead investigate the processes and causes that produce structures; avoid anthropomorphic or purpose-driven reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigate underlying chemical processes for adaptive responses
rubrics_metrics.description: An investigation of the real underlying conditions which govern such a modified reaction would be of immense value ... the information we might gain ... would prove to be of first-rate importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When observing adaptive responses (e.g., cork formation after wounding), pursue experiments and analyses to uncover the chemical/metabolic bases rather than stopping at functional descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use empirical taxonomic characters cautiously; seek physico-chemical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: When we desire to know the taxonomic value of this or that character, we are perforce largely guided by purely empirical considerations ... when we do [know], I am convinced that the reason will be found to lie in chemical and physical causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Empirically useful morphological characters should be interpreted in light of underlying physico-chemical causes; their taxonomic reliability may vary across groups and should be investigated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test mechanisms by experimental manipulation (diffusion, nutriment, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the nutriment agar be kept fairly dry, so that the rate of diffusion of soluble materials is slowed down, it is found that concentric zones of sterile and sporiferous hyphae regularly alternate ... interference with the circular form of zones ... by artificially interfering with the rate of diffusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use controlled manipulations (e.g., diffusion rate, moisture, nutrient supply) to test mechanistic hypotheses about observed patterns (e.g., fairy-rings, zonation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for physico-chemical factors in cellular reactions (diffusion, adsorption, surface-tension, electrical relations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Questions of rates of diffusion, physical absorption, and the like have to be taken into account; and beyond all these there remain the series of remarkable electrical relations which the proteins exhibit, as well as those changes in surface-tension ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experimental and interpretive work at the cellular level must consider diffusion rates, adsorption phenomena, surface-tension changes, and electrochemical context (electrolytes, ionic dissociation) as potentially decisive factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validate histological preparations against living patterns and fixation fidelity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided we have sufficiently good grounds for enabling us to feel confident that the precipitation or coagulation faithfully maps out the positions originally occupied by the respective colloids during life, there is no real force in the objection [to histological methods].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use living observations and experiments on artificial mixtures to test whether fixing/staining faithfully represent in vivo distributions; when validated, histology remains a reliable method despite representing precipitates/coagulates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study electrical/physico-chemical changes in nuclear division and chromosomal behaviour
rubrics_metrics.description: We have also, I believe, evidence of physical disturbances of an electrical nature which accompany, and indeed in a measure determine, the course of mitosis ... indicated ... by the remarkable alterations in surface-tension exhibited by the nuclear membrane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigations of mitosis should include measurement/consideration of electrical charges, induced charges, surface-tension changes, and the physicochemical behaviour of proteins and nucleins to better understand mechanics of nuclear events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise institutional resource requirements for university quality
rubrics_metrics.description: The greatest peril to university education in South Africa lies in the excessive multiplication of institutions with poor endowment and small, underpaid, and overworked staffs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: University quality depends on adequate endowment, appropriate staff size and pay, and avoidance of fragmented expansion into under-resourced institutions; institutional policy should prioritise sustainable resourcing.
